references.text: Terah's genealogy leading up to his three sons Abram, Nahor, and Haran, forming the direct context for the family tree in verse 27.
Terah took Abram, Lot (Haran's son), and Sarai from Ur of the Chaldeans toward Canaan, but they settled in Haran. This continues the story of Terah's family.
The Lord calls Abram to leave his land and his kindred – this is the next major step in the story after the introduction of Terah's family.
Abram went out as the Lord had said, taking Lot, Haran's son, with him. Lot was introduced as Haran's son in 11:27.
Joshua mentions that Terah, the father of Abraham and Nahor, lived on the other side of the river and served other gods – a direct reference to Terah's family.
By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out. This connects with Abram, who is introduced here as Terah's son.
Direct narrative continuation: 11:27 establishes Lot's lineage, while 12:5 shows his role in Abraham's journey.
